Arvind’s proposed ₹100 crore (~$11 million) Varanasi garment unit is nearing commissioning, with inauguration proposed for October 25, 2026.
The project is expected to employ over 1,000 people, but disclosures by October 23 had not confirmed commercial production, capacity or final products.
PLI or Uttar Pradesh incentive approval is unproven; orders, costs and utilisation will shape its impact.

title: South Indian cotton yarn sentiment improves, Mumbai prices rise
summary:
South India’s cotton market firmed, with Mumbai cotton yarn prices rising ₹3–5 (~$0.03–0.05) per kg as costlier cotton lifted spinning mills’ sentiment, while Tiruppur held steady.
Traders expect downstream demand to improve after Diwali, though payment constraints and possible yarn dispatch disruptions remain concerns.
Gujarat cotton gained ₹100–200 per candy on slow arrivals after erratic rainfall.

title: Nigeria’s $1.122 bn textile import market: Can local mills compete?
summary:
TexPro records Nigerian textile imports across HS 50-63 at $421.2 million in H1 2026, up 16.2 per cent from $362.6 million in H1 2025.
Across January 2025-June 2026, imports total $1.122 billion, with man-made fibres accounting for $608 million, or 54 per cent.
China is the largest supplier at $629 million, 56 per cent of the dataset, ahead of Japan, Vietnam, Turkiye, Kenya and India.

title: Bangladesh’s $9.17 bn non-cotton shift meets a $2.43 bn input bill
summary:
Non-cotton apparel made up 30.7 per cent of Bangladesh’s $29.91 billion garment exports in January to September 2026, but TexPro data show uneven diversification.
Selected fibre, yarn and fabric imports rose 4.6 per cent to $2.43 billion in H1, with China supplying 81.3 per cent.
Energy shortages, woven gaps and planned polyester-chip capacity will shape where value is captured.

title: India to fund micro & small exporters' certification under EPM: Goyal
summary:
India will cover the full cost of expensive certifications for micro and small enterprises under the Export Promotion Mission, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said. 
Support will also cover EU compliance, including CBAM and EUDR, helping exporters ease testing, certification, emissions-monitoring and traceability costs and improve global competitiveness.

title: Drewry WCI gains 2.2% amid higher Asia-Europe shipping rates
summary:
Drewry’s World Container Index rose 2.2 per cent to $4,585 per FEU in the week ending October 22, driven by higher Asia–Europe rates.
Shanghai-Rotterdam rates rose 3 per cent and Shanghai-Genoa 5 per cent, while Transpacific rates gained on US import demand.
Asia–Europe blank sailings rise next week, Asian port congestion eases and Gulf security risks keep the East-West outlook uncertain.

title: ACIMIT reports textile machinery orders up 7% in Q3 2026
summary:
Italian textile machinery orders rose 7 per cent year on year in Q3 2026, driven by an 8 per cent increase in foreign demand, while domestic orders fell 4 per cent.
Overall intake declined 4 per cent from Q2, reflecting investment uncertainty.
Capacity utilisation stood at 72.4 per cent, with a 3.5-month backlog.
ACIMIT reported cautious Q4 expectations amid rising energy costs and weak domestic demand.

title: EU workwear imports Hit €3.4 bn: Why low cost isn’t enough?
summary:
Europe’s workwear market is rewarding apparel suppliers that can prove safety performance, repeatable quality and reliable replenishment, not just low prices.
EU workwear imports reached €3.4 billion (~$3.82 billion) in 2024, while broader woven-apparel imports rose to $44.64 billion in 2025.
Tunisia led non-EU workwear suppliers; India’s opportunity depends on certification, lead times and EU rules.

title: EU agrees to raise carbon market reserve cap to 700 mn allowances
summary:
The European Commission has welcomed a provisional European Parliament-Council agreement to strengthen the Market Stability Reserve of the EU Emissions Trading System.
The deal would let the reserve retain up to 700 million allowances, compared with invalidating holdings above 400 million under current rules.
Formal adoption is still required before the amendment enters into force.

title: US cotton export sales surge 36%, Vietnam leads buying
summary:
US Upland cotton export sales rose 36 per cent to 199,600 RB in the week ended October 15, with shipments up 40 per cent to 196,400 RB, USDA data showed.
Vietnam led purchases at 94,500 RB, followed by Bangladesh, Turkiye, Pakistan and India, as Asian textile-producing markets drove the rebound.
Pima cotton demand weakened, with sales down 81 per cent and exports down 28 per cent.

title: EU seizes record 196 mn counterfeits worth $7.1 bn; clothing tops list
summary:
EU authorities seized a record 196 million counterfeit items worth €6.3 billion ($7.1 billion) in 2025, up 67 per cent from 2024, the European Commission said. 
Clothing accounted for nearly one-fifth of detained items. 
Customs intercepted 42 million goods at EU borders, with most cases linked to express courier and postal shipments associated with e-commerce.

title: Bangladesh apparel exports to EU fall 11.4%: What drives the drop?
summary:
TexPro data show Bangladesh apparel export value for HS 61 and HS 62 to EU destinations fell 11.43 per cent in January–August 2026.
Values declined 4.31 per cent to the United States, 0.61 per cent to the United Kingdom and 7.69 per cent worldwide.
Eurostat data show EU apparel imports from Bangladesh fell 11.67 per cent; buyers should prepare for the EU’s post-transition preference framework.

title: US’ Deckers Brands' Q2 profit rises 17% as Hoka, UGG expand
summary:
Deckers Brands has raised its FY27 diluted earnings per share outlook after second-quarter earnings exceeded expectations, supported by disciplined marketplace management and expense control. 
Second-quarter net sales rose 3.5 per cent to $1.48 billion, while net income increased 17 per cent to $313.1 million. 
Tariff refunds lifted margins and EPS, as Hoka and UGG both delivered sales growth.

title: Georgia's apparel imports rise 14%, European suppliers gain share
summary:
Georgia's apparel imports rose 13.96 per cent to $289.759 million in January–August 2026, with Europe strengthening its lead as the largest supplier.
European shipments grew 17.64 per cent to $128.148 million, lifting share to 44.23 per cent, while Asia-Pacific's share fell to 24.43 per cent.
Turkiye, China, Spain, Italy and Germany remained the top five suppliers.

title: Taiwan's Fulgent Sun's Q3 revenue rises 42%
summary:
Taiwanese footwear OEM Fulgent Sun’s FY26 Q3 revenue rose 42.32 per cent year on year to NT$5.44 billion (~$167.84 million), supported by added capacity. 
Operating profit fell 23.74 per cent and net income attributable to owners dropped 54.68 per cent despite higher gross profit. 
Margins narrowed on tariffs, raw-material volatility, wage rises, start-up costs at new plants and foreign-exchange impact.

title: US' UniFirst FY26 revenue rises as merger costs curb profit
summary:
UniFirst Corporation recorded fiscal 2026 revenue of $2.52 billion, up 3.7 per cent, supported by growth across its operating segments. 
Net income fell to $109.5 million as proposed Cintas merger and enterprise resource planning costs weighed on earnings. 
Fourth-quarter revenue rose 5 per cent to $645 million, while adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 14.7 per cent.

title: US apparel imports from Peru fall 10.4% as supplier trends diverge
summary:
Peruvian exporters must factor a 12.5 per cent US Section 301 duty into covered US-bound apparel shipments, as Peru’s free-trade agreement does not remove the new charge.
US exemptions apply only to qualifying USMCA and CAFTA-DR textile and apparel entries.
US apparel imports fell 7.4 per cent to about $49.08 billion in January-August 2026, with supplier performance diverging.

title: From online hype to profit: Why India’s apparel brands need stores
summary:
India’s D2C apparel websites account for only $3.3 billion, or 3.4 per cent, of the country’s $95.7 billion domestic apparel market in 2025.
Offline channels still hold 83 per cent of sales, while marketplaces take about 80 per cent of online apparel sales, CMAI and 1Lattice found.
Rahul Mehta says brands need customer data, stores and profitability as consolidation looms.

title: Germany's Adidas raises 2026 profit outlook to $2.81 bn
summary:
Adidas raised its 2026 operating profit outlook to €2.5 billion (~$2.81 billion) after record Q3 results.
Revenue rose 9 per cent to €7.252 billion (~$8.14 billion), while operating profit climbed 37 per cent to €1.008 billion (~$1.13 billion). 
Full-price sales and a US tariff refund supported margins, with fourth-quarter investment planned to strengthen future profitability.

title: New Zealand's apparel imports rise 5.9% in September 2026
summary:
New Zealand's apparel imports rose 5.9 per cent year on year to NZ$190.20 million ($107.85 million) in September, a third straight monthly gain.
January–September imports were virtually flat at NZ$1.567 billion, with knitted apparel up 0.7 per cent and non-knitted down 0.8 per cent.
Exports fell 2.6 per cent to NZ$18.52 million in September, as knitted apparel shipments dropped but non-knitted exports rose.
